summary.intent: Get two outstanding Callisto PRs (#242 onboarding / #634 and #246 interactive add-init / #638) to a mergeable state with no further review findings, by fixing the underlying architectural patterns rather than spot-fixing each reviewer finding.
summary.outcome: Pivoted to boundary-level fixes: #242's URL changes were reverted and pushed (1abf4f227), the Git boundary work (#494, slice A pushed, slice B in progress) was started, and #246 moved to a line-based picker. Independent whole-PR reviews and delta reviews found only low items, which were being fixed; the full gate passed on both, but final pushes of #634 and #638 were not yet done.

repo: Local Git access goes through the GitAccess boundary in callisto-model, but remote access had no model. Raw URL strings were parsed and rewritten with url::Url across callisto-graph, which caused the recurring URL/git findings.

Planned fix: a GitRemote type that calls Git by remote name (push origin, ls-remote origin) and fingerprints Git's own get-url output. Also Rev, a single GitPath, git add moved inside GitAccess, and one central Git environment policy.
CommandRunner is the single test seam, so no new trait is needed for the Git boundary.

Prompt design decision (final): unbounded lists are printed once as plain text and answered via inquire's one-line Text prompt. There is no custom terminal code, and findings about inquire's internal behaviour (resize, pane size, keys) are dismissed with a documented limit.
Changesets v3 uses @clack/prompts as shipped and builds no terminal handling of its own. Callisto's wins are around the widget: preselected changed packages, a review step, clean non-TTY errors.
Registry URLs in E120 show only scheme and host on purpose, because some registries (Gemfury) put tokens in the path. The message should point to where to compare instead.
The rustix dev-dependency needs both the pty and termios features in callisto-cli because the pty tests call tcsetwinsize; crossterm only enables termios incidentally.

code.finding: The hint text depends on marked rows and the empty_ok flag. The first list passes false and the bump lists pass true, so an empty Enter on the first list becomes E273.
position() matches the first package whose name or qualified id equals the typed word, so a duplicate match silently goes to the first row.
review() now escapes package names with escape_debug(), matching print_list, so control characters in names can't drive the terminal.
E342 returns before the Changesets migration warnings are queued, so they are dropped. The fix is to extend notes right after changesets::migrate.
ShownRegistry::new strips the registry URL down to scheme and host. This hides the differing path, but it is kept deliberately for security.

workflow: Findings should be triaged by class and owning boundary, with a codebase-wide sweep, before any fix is briefed. Treating each reviewer finding as a lone to-do caused the endless loop.
The user rejected hand-maintained ledgers and a push-gate hook as ceremony, so the commitment is recorded in memory and the audit is run by agents.
Converge locally (audit, fix, audit until clean) before one push. An independent whole-PR review plus a delta review of the final batch catches issues before the paid reviewer does.
Subagent reports are treated as input, not authority. Security-relevant suggestions (showing the full registry path) were overridden with reasoning.
Report only gate exit codes actually observed, and don't promise zero future findings.

friction: The same URL/git findings kept recurring on #242 across about 13 findings, because each fix re-implemented Git's resolution differently.
Flip-flopping on #246 between a checkbox widget, sizing, truncation, hand-built termios, and inquire; #246 had more findings after a push than before.
The user repeatedly said they had asked for pattern-level analysis, felt ignored, and was frustrated by repeated findings.
The #242 fix session ended without committing, likely blocked by the ledger rule lacking rows for new findings.
The user questioned whether ledgers and hooks were human bureaucracy, and asked for speed and token efficiency alongside quality.
open_items: Git boundary slice B (Rev, one GitPath, git add inside the boundary) is in progress in session c7dc84c2 on trail #494.
#634 final batch of 7 low fixes still needs to be committed, its convergence record written, and the push done, then its findings resolved.
#638 follow-ups (termios feature, collision message) are committed or in progress and need a push after delta review, then resolving 3 findings. The five-item batch is done.
Pending contract decisions for the owner: TERM=dumb never prompts, init context to stderr while prompting, and re-asking on an empty selection instead of E273.
